# Fixtures

Real image files, committed as binaries rather than generated at test time. A
generated fixture would change whenever the generator changed, which is exactly
when a codec regression is easiest to miss.

| File | What it is | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `photo.jpg` | 1200×800, JPEG q92, smooth gradients plus per-pixel noise | Stands in for a photograph: lossy source, lossy target |
| `flat.png` | 640×480, four flat colours on a light ground | The case OxiPNG wins on, and where lossless has to stay lossless |
| `broken.jpg` | A valid JPEG header followed by 70 bytes of text | Proves one damaged file is skipped with a warning rather than failing the run |

`photo.jpg` and `flat.png` were produced once with `System.Drawing` on Windows;
`broken.jpg` was written by hand. Regenerating them is not part of the test run.

**`photo.jpg` is synthetic and flatters the encoders.** Its gradients are exactly
what AVIF is best at, so it compresses far harder than a real photograph would.
The tests assert direction and bounds — smaller, decodable, correct dimensions —
never a specific ratio. Do not quote numbers measured on it as product claims.

EXIF-bearing and metadata-bearing variants are built inside `tests/unit/metadata.test.ts`
by splicing real segments into these files, so the exact bytes under test are
visible in the test rather than hidden in a binary.

## Fonts

`fonts/plex-mono.*` is IBM Plex Mono, Regular, Latin subset, under the SIL Open
Font License — the licence is alongside them in `fonts/OFL.txt`. The `.woff` and
`.woff2` came from the `@fontsource/ibm-plex-mono` package; the `.ttf` is the
`.woff2` decompressed, so all three are the same outlines in three containers.

**It is already a single-script subset**, which makes it a deliberately
unflattering fixture for range splitting: there is almost nothing to split. That
is the point — it keeps the split-mode numbers honest. Codepoint subsetting on the
same file gives around 82%.

Note the `.woff` and `.woff2` builds do not carry an identical table set: the
WOFF2 keeps the hinting tables (`cvt `, `fpgm`, `prep`) and the WOFF does not. The
tests check for the tables a font must have rather than asserting the two are
equal.

## Text

`text/` holds one file per type the Phase 3 pipeline handles. They are written to
be *hostile to an over-eager minifier*, and every oddity in them is load-bearing:

| File | What it is testing |
|---|---|
| `site.css` | a rule referenced by no HTML we supply, which must survive (ADR-002) |
| `app.js` | a classic script whose top-level names are globals and must keep them |
| `module.mjs` | a real module, where mangling local names *is* safe |
| `page.html` | attributes an aggressive minifier drops, and a word gap between two inline elements |
| `logo.svg` | viewBox, `<title>`, `<desc>`, ids, an unreferenced def, a hidden group and an empty one |

Do not tidy these files. Removing the "pointless" empty attribute or the unused
CSS rule removes the test.

## Site

`site/` is a small but deliberately awkward website, used by the folder-mode and
Law 3 suites. Every reference in it is there to exercise one branch of "may this
file be renamed?":

| File | What it proves |
|---|---|
| `img/icon.png` | referenced only in resolvable ways, so it *is* fingerprinted |
| `img/inline.png` | reached from an inline `style` attribute — never renamed |
| `img/scripted.png` | named inside `js/app.js` — never renamed, because scripts are not rewritten |
| `index.html` | holds a templated `src`, an external URL, and a two-candidate `srcset` |
| `about.html` | holds a `<style>` block, which *is* rewritable, unlike a style attribute |
| `css/site.css` | `@import`, `../` relative paths, and one `url()` pointing at a file that does not exist |

Both pages are also rendered by the verifier at three viewports, so the fixture
doubles as the Phase 5 test site.

Do not "fix" the broken reference or remove the templated one. They are the tests.

## Added for ADR-026

| File | Source |
|---|---|
| `photo.heic` | `examples/example.heic` from the libheif project (strukturag/libheif), the library Pare uses to decode HEIC. 1280×854. |
| `gradient-24.bmp`, `palette-8.bmp`, `alpha-32.bmp` | Generated by `scripts/make-bmp-fixtures.mjs`: 24-bit, 8-bit palette, and 32-bit with real alpha, 64×48. |

## Added for the privacy mark (audit item 5)

| File | Source |
|---|---|
| `gps.jpg` | `photo.jpg` with an EXIF APP1 segment holding a GPS directory (latitude 51°30′ N) inserted after SOI. Built by hand: a big-endian TIFF block, IFD0 with one GPS pointer, a GPS directory with LatitudeRef and Latitude. |
